ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.07 (voucher) for the non-exempt portion of the 09:20–09:26 detour; no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI trip, metered fare $45.04 [F7]: the only question is how much of the single off-route segment 09:20–09:26 [F3] is refundable under RD-2, because one segment exists and no incident exempts it [RD-1][F15]. The RD-4 screen fails — no qualifying LTA incident, and a speed band alone does not exempt [RD-4][F12][F15].

The rider's message was sent at 09:18, before the segment began at 09:20 [F8][F9][F3], so timing satisfies RD-5. Its words, however, are a general route choice: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F9] is the driver's invitation "want me to take another way?" [F8] answered with a general authorisation, not the naming of any road. Under RD-5(1) a general authorisation covers a route chosen to get to the destination, and the driver's own statement frames what he did as a route — "so I went round" on the jams [F11] — nothing in the record shows an errand of the driver's own, a stop or a loop that reaches nothing. The vehicle was measured up to 1027 m off the optimal route and arrived at Changi T3 [F3][F1], i.e. the segment was part of getting there, not a detour for the driver's benefit.

But a general authorisation must still be exercised as the faster way, and the record shows the substitution did not beat the route it replaced: the jam on East Coast Parkway was band 2 only for 08:58–09:20 [F12], i.e. it was clearing just as the detour began at 09:20 [F3], and the trip took 35.4 min against 25.2 min estimated and 21.6 km against 19.3 km [F2][F1]. The detour's first 1.86 km is what the optimal route itself would have covered at that point, and only that stretch is explained by the agreed substitution [RD-5][F3]; the remaining 2.18 km is unattributed [RD-1][F3][F9]. The general consent therefore covers 1.86 km of the 4.04 km segment, leaving 2.18 km as a non-exempt deviation [RD-2][F3][F9].

Amount: $30.46 ÷ 21.60 km = $1.4102/km [F4][F7]; 2.18 km × $1.4102/km = $3.07. Note the billed excess of 2.35 km/$3.31 [F4] exceeds the measured 2.18 km because the corridor tolerance and matching noise are not refunded [RD-2]. Waiting fee $0.11 is a metered waiting unit and is not refunded [F5][F7][RD-3(c)]. Safety screen: no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the chat, the driver's statement or the complaint — the messages are a route arrangement and an apology for lateness [F8][F9][F11], so no escalation [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. No prior upheld route dispute in 90 days [F18], so RD-6 does not attach [RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: Rider's 09:18 message "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F9], sent before the segment start 09:20 [F3], is a general route choice answering the driver's offer to take another way [F8], and the driver's statement confirms he went round on the jams rather than on an errand of his own [F11]. A general authorisation covers only the route chosen to get there and must still be the faster way; the ECP jam was band 2 only 08:58–09:20, clearing as the detour began [F12], and the vehicle ran up to 1027 m off the optimal route for 4.04 km against 1.86 km [F3], longer than the trip should take [F1][F2]. The 1.86 km the optimal route itself covered is explained, but 2.18 km of the segment is not, so the non-exempt 2.18 km counts for refund [RD-2][RD-1]. Timing alone does not extend consent past the substitution actually agreed.
